charleston-south-carolina.file_title: File:Rainbow Row, South of Broad, Charleston, SC (49477988853).jpg
charleston-south-carolina.author: Warren LeMay from Covington, KY, United States
charleston-south-carolina.alt: Rainbow Row in Charleston: a pink three-storey house with black shutters and a small iron balcony, then lavender and green houses among palmetto trees, under a blue sky.
charleston-south-carolina.why: Charleston without parked cars across the foreground (the round-4 review's R20: Rainbow Row behind parked cars, an SUV foremost). Rainbow Row is Charleston's most recognised street, and every view of it found has cars at the curb; this one, under a clear October sky, puts them along the bottom edge, so at 50% 15% the band and the link preview show none and the card the top of one. 3642px wide; the 1920px rendition applied.
charleston-south-carolina.checked: the pink, lavender and green houses of Rainbow Row, palmettos, a street lamp; no person; no sculpture or mural; no logo or sign of note; parked cars along the bottom edge (a black SUV, two sedans), outside the band's and the link preview's crops at 50% 15% and the top of one on the 16:10 card

alternatives.author: Thomson200
alternatives.note: the current photograph, focused higher (50% 10%): the band shows the houses and palms without the cars, the card still has them; an overcast sky

alternatives.author: John Hoey from Framingham, MA, United States
alternatives.note: no cars: a close view of a yellow façade with window boxes and the shaded sidewalk; reads less surely as Rainbow Row

york-pennsylvania.author: Acroterion
york-pennsylvania.alt: York's Central Market House, a red-brick market hall with two slate-roofed towers, a central gable and green arched doors, under a cloud-streaked sky.
york-pennsylvania.why: York at the city band's width (the round-4 review's R20: the photograph, a blossoming downtown street, is 1024px wide, upscaled in the 1,056px band; Commons holds nothing larger of it). The Central Market House (on the National Register of Historic Places, as its file page notes) is downtown York's best-known building; June 2022, 5540px wide, the 1920px rendition applied. At 50% 20% the band and the link preview show the building without the cars parked at its curb.
york-pennsylvania.checked: the market house's brick front, towers and doors, row houses either side; one small figure at a door, none as the subject; no sculpture or mural; its own name in small letters over the doors, no logo; cars parked along the bottom edge, outside the band's and the link preview's crops at 50% 20%, small on the 16:10 card

alternatives.author: Lincolnman65
alternatives.note: the current photograph's kind, a downtown street under white blossom, at 2668px; busier, with cars in the card

reno-nevada.file_title: File:View of Reno, Nevada from Juniper Ridge (20720895303).jpg
reno-nevada.author: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA
reno-nevada.alt: Downtown Reno's casino and hotel towers above a broad canopy of green trees, with brown hills and mountains behind.
reno-nevada.why: Reno at the city band's width (the round-4 review's R20: the photograph, the skyline at golden hour, is 900px wide, upscaled in the band since round 3; Commons holds nothing larger of it). The same view of downtown's towers under the hills, from Juniper Ridge on a June evening in daylight, 4000px wide, the 1920px rendition applied; the default focus keeps the towers in every crop.
reno-nevada.checked: downtown's towers, the hills and mountains behind, trees in front; no person; no sculpture or mural; the casinos' names on their towers small, as in any view of Reno's skyline, none as the subject

fargo-north-dakota.why: The band read "FARG" (the round-4 review's R20, known since round 3): at Phase 6's 50% 20% the band's lower edge cut the sign's last letter. Checked on the page itself at 1440, 1024 and 390: at 50% 36% the band holds the whole vertical FARGO, the card and the link preview the whole sign and the marquee. The photograph stays.

peoria-illinois.why: The round-4 review (R20) offered leaving it (a bank's octagonal logo is the brightest mark on its skyline; logos are part of any skyline) or a view from the bluffs, only if clearly better. None was: the other downtown views across the river show the same logo, and the views from the bluffs (Grandview Drive) show the Illinois River valley without the city.
